name: Nantes
description: City on the River Loire, political and ecclesiastical center and capital of the duchy of Brittany; its cathedral is a site of martyrdom from 843.

name: County of Nantes
description: Breton county around Nantes with few Bretons and a Frankish population feeling affinity with Anjou and Poitou.

name: Brittany
description: Duchy bordering Normandy to the south; Nantes is its capital.

name: Blain
description: Place where two minor trade routes cross, with a small castle and busy market.

name: Gâvre Forest
description: Forest near Blain in which a leper hospital is hidden.

name: Redon
description: Highest port on the River Vilaine accessible to sea-going craft, site of the Abbey of St. Savior and a trade distribution point.

name: Abbey of St. Savior
description: Abbey at Redon established in 832.

name: St. Just
description: Village north of Redon near which groups of gray stones lie in a level 3 Magic aura.

name: Grande Brière
description: Immense peat marsh between the Loire and Vilaine estuaries, rich in fish, eels and wildfowl but scarcely inhabited.

name: Kerbourg
description: Patch of firm ground in the Grande Brière with a covered alley of megaliths in a low Magic aura.

name: Ranrouët
description: Fortress under construction guarding the north side of the Grande Brière marsh.

name: Guérande
description: Settlement overlooking the Brière marsh with the church of St. Aubin, built on a baptistery site; salt is extracted nearby.

name: Alain Crookbeard
description: Breton king who established Nantes as the capital of the duchy.

name: River Loire
description: Major river flowing through Nantes, Anjou and Tours; chief route for trade and travel in Anjou.

name: River Vilaine
description: Breton river whose highest sea-going port is Redon.

name: Normandy
description: Duchy bounded by the English Channel, annexed by Philip II in 1203-1204; heavily forested with many castles.

name: Normandy Tribunal
description: The Hermetic Tribunal covering Normandy and much of France, including northern Aquitaine.

name: England
description: Kingdom across the Channel conquered by the Normans in 1066, a military foe of France.

name: Secunda Provincia Lugdunensis
description: Roman province corresponding to Normandy, whose chief city was Rotomagus.

name: Neustria
description: Carolingian province that included Normandy and was overrun by Vikings in the ninth and tenth centuries.

name: Vikings
description: Scandinavian raiders who overran Neustria and colonized Normandy; their leader became duke.

name: Philip II
description: King of France who annexed Normandy in 1203-1204 and took Anjou and Tours; delegates authority to bailli.

name: Henry III
description: King of England, Anglo-Norman claimant to Normandy and present Duke of Aquitaine.

name: King John
description: King John of England, who granted many small Norman town charters before 1204 and lost Anjou to Philip II.

name: Confluensis
description: Large Quaesitorial covenant on the Cotentin peninsula, current Normandy covenant, on the site of the Orchard of Sour Apples.

name: Dragon's Rest
description: Current Normandy covenant at the mouth of the Seine.

name: Montverte
description: Venerable Autumn covenant in southern Normandy, one of the five great lieges, known for Hermetic raiding and dominating the Baron of Montverte.

name: Aedes Salii
description: Ruined Normandy covenant, a vassal of Sinapis.

name: Baiocassium
description: Ruined Diedne covenant in the forest of Bayeux.

name: Baiocassium Minor
description: Lost Diedne vassal covenant rumored to lie in a regio within the town of Bayeux.

name: Orchard of Sour Apples
description: Lost covenant whose site is now occupied by Confluensis.

name: Pagus
description: Covenant near Cherbourg destroyed during the Schism War; its vis sources are claimed by a Fengheld chapterhouse.

name: Rotomagus
description: Covenant briefly sited near Rouen in the ninth century, named after the Roman town.

name: Bailli
description: Professional royal bureaucrats appointed by Philip II to administer bailliages in Normandy and Anjou.

name: Jean de la Porte
description: Bailli of Rouen, appointed 1219.

name: Pierre du Thillai
description: Bailli of Caen, appointed 1205.

name: Renaud de Ville-Thierry
description: Bailli of Bayeux, appointed 1206.

name: Miles de Levis
description: Bailli of Cotentin, appointed 1215.

name: Order of Hermes
description: The order of Hermetic magi, known to the Norman bailli and bishops; the archbishop of Rouen believes it heretical.

name: Town Charter
description: Grant allowing town burgesses to elect mayors and hold courts in return for collective tenure; many Norman towns have them.

name: Beauvoir
description: Small chartered forest community in Normandy.

name: Laigle
description: Small chartered forest community in Normandy.

name: Trun
description: Small chartered forest community in Normandy.

name: Conches
description: Chartered village outside an abbey in Normandy.

name: Lyre
description: Chartered village outside an abbey in Normandy.

name: Saint-Evroult
description: Chartered village outside an abbey in Normandy.

name: Claville
description: Chartered community in Normandy that is really a large manor.

name: Archdiocese of Rouen
description: Archdiocese whose borders nearly match the duchy of Normandy, raised to an archdiocese in 744.

name: Nicaise
description: First bishop of Rouen, martyred in the mid-third century.

name: St. Mellon
description: Successor of Nicaise who established the diocese of Rouen.

name: Robert Poulain
description: Archbishop of Rouen, a theologian elected 1208, who believes the Order of Hermes heretical.

name: Thibaud d'Amiens
description: Historical successor to the archbishop of Rouen in 1222.

name: Robert des Ablèges
description: Theologian bishop of Bayeux, elected 1206.

name: Hugh Neret
description: Canonist bishop of Coutances, elected 1208.

name: William du Pont-de-l'Arche
description: Canonist bishop of Lisieux, elected 1218.

name: William d'Ostilly
description: Bishop of Avranches, a local dean elected 1212.

name: Luke of Evreux
description: Bishop of Evreux elected 1203, who historically dies in 1220.

name: Sylvester of Sées
description: Bishop of Sées elected 1201, formerly archdeacon; historically dies in 1220.

name: Gervase of Chichester
description: Foreign candidate favored by the papacy, elected to Sées after Sylvester.

name: Ralph de Cierrey
description: Local dean elected bishop of Evreux after Luke.

name: The Vacant Castle
description: Vacant castle on the Cotentin peninsula lair of a Grendel-kin monster and holding a strong Magic aura; proposed site for a new covenant.

name: Grendel
description: Monster of the Beowulf saga; the Vacant Castle monster is related to it.

name: Lutin
description: Servile faerie goblins of Normandy (Faerie Might 5 Aquam) that clean households for offerings and dread a 'goblin duke of Normandy'.

name: The Master's Things
description: Lutin power granting awareness of every item in the room it occupies.

name: Soap and Suds
description: Lutin Aquam power making the floor of a room soapy and slippery.

name: Goblin Duke of Normandy
description: Mysterious figure universally dreaded by lutin, unknown to the Order.

name: St. Ouen
description: Canonized bishop of Rouen (641-684) who converted or exterminated many pagans.

name: St. Victricius
description: Bishop and theological writer at Rouen (380-409), author of De Laude Sanctorum and Liber Regularum.

name: De Laude Sanctorum
description: Theology summa (Quality 11, Level 5) by St. Victricius kept at Rouen Cathedral.

name: Liber Regularum
description: Civil and Canon Law summa (Quality 10, Level 3) by St. Victricius.

name: Hugh of Amiens
description: Theological writer (1130-74), author of Contra Haereticos.

name: Contra Haereticos
description: Divine Lore summa by Hugh of Amiens compiled with an Infernal Lore tractatus.

name: Rouen Cathedral
description: Seat of the archdiocese at Rouen, holding saints' writings and the tombs of Norman nobles including Rollo.

name: Seine River
description: River linking Paris to the coast; its basin is the productive heart of Normandy.

name: Forest of Lyons
description: Remnant forest favored for hunting by Norman nobles; a castle at its heart eliminated its forest spirit.

name: Bocage
description: Norman practice of dividing fields with low stone walls into small allotments.

name: Rouen
description: Capital of Normandy on the Seine, Roman Rotomagus, captured by Philip II in 1203; has a cathedral and a declining Jewish community.

name: Rollo
description: Viking chieftain interred in Rouen Cathedral; distant relative of Haland and Harivald.

name: Gargouille
description: Scaled magical beast from the Seine defeated in the seventh century by St. Romanus with the sign of the cross.

name: St. Romanus
description: Archbishop of Rouen who paralyzed the Gargouille; his shrine has a Faith Point total of 5.

name: Shrine of St. Romanus
description: Relic shrine of St. Romanus with a Faith Point total of 5, carried by the archbishop in a story seed.

name: Jumieges
description: Benedictine abbey on the Seine founded 634 by St. Philibert, a major center of scholarship with over 1,000 monks.

name: St. Philibert
description: Founder of the abbey of Jumieges in 634.

name: St. Wandrille
description: Large Benedictine abbey downstream of Jumieges; its monks colonized Mont St. Michael in 966.

name: Historia rerum Anglicarum
description: History by William of Newburgh with Area Lore: England summa and Area Lore: Normandy tractatus.

name: William of Newburgh
description: Historian (1136-1198), author of Historia rerum Anglicarum.

name: The Ecclesiastical History
description: History by Orderic Vitalis including Area Lore summae and a Civil and Canon Law tractatus.

name: Orderic Vitalis
description: Historian (1075-1141), author of The Ecclesiastical History.

name: Historia Normannorum
description: History by William of Jumieges with an Area Lore: Normandy summa.

name: William of Jumieges
description: Historian (1025-1090), author of Historia Normannorum.

name: History of the Normans
description: History by Dudo of St Quentin containing Area Lore: Normandy summa and tractatus.

name: Dudo of St Quentin
description: Historian (960-1025), author of History of the Normans.

name: County of Bayeux
description: Forested county west of the Seine basin, with the towns of Caen and Bayeux and the ruined covenant Baiocassium.

name: Diocese of Bayeux
description: One of the oldest dioceses in Mythic Europe, founded by St. Exuperius.

name: St. Exuperius
description: Founder of the Diocese of Bayeux in the first century.

name: St. Vigor
description: Bishop of Bayeux who destroyed a pagan temple in the sixth century, earning the enmity of the faeries.

name: Odo of Conteville
description: Bishop of Bayeux and brother of William the Conqueror who commissioned the Bayeux tapestry.

name: William the Conqueror
description: Duke of Normandy who conquered England in 1066; his corpse is said to hold a trapped demon.

name: Bayeux
description: Town, once Gallic Baiocasses, with Bayeux Cathedral and mills; rumored to hide the regio of Baiocassium Minor.

name: Bayeux Tapestry
description: Embroidery commissioned by Odo depicting Harold; magic woven into it gives a +2 Sympathetic Connection to the Duke of Normandy and King of England.

name: Bayeux Cathedral
description: Cathedral in Bayeux storing the tapestry.

name: Harold
description: King of England depicted on the Bayeux tapestry, killed by the Normans.

name: Caen
description: Town on the River Orne, William the Conqueror's effective capital, dominated by Caen Castle.

name: Caen Castle
description: Enormous fortress begun in 1060, recently extended by Philip II.

name: Men's Abbey
description: Fortified abbey in Caen built by William the Conqueror, site of his botched funeral.

name: Women's Abbey
description: Fortified abbey in Caen built by Matilda.

name: Matilda
description: Wife and cousin of William the Conqueror who built the Women's Abbey.

name: Pope Nicholas II
description: Pope who excommunicated William and Matilda for being cousins.

name: White Ladies
description: Coterie of Sidhe fay, reputed sisters of the Lady of the Lake, who rule faerie regiones near Bayeux and seek dancing partners.

name: Lady of the Lake
description: Arthurian figure whose sisters are reputed to be the white ladies.

name: Cotentin Peninsula
description: Lightly settled, swampy region of Normandy containing Confluensis and the ruins of Pagus.

name: Forest of Brix
description: Forest south of Cherbourg haunted by packs of faerie wolves.

name: Faerie Wolves
description: Ferocious packs of faerie wolves haunting the forest of Brix.

name: Cherbourg
description: Town on the Cotentin near the ruined covenant Pagus, with a Fengheld chapterhouse.

name: Fengheld
description: Large Rhine Tribunal covenant with a chapterhouse in Cherbourg claiming Pagus' vis sources.

name: Rhine Tribunal
description: Tribunal containing Fengheld and Waddenzee.

name: Schism War
description: Hermetic conflict in which Pagus was destroyed and Montverte slew many Diedne.

name: The Infernal Grave of William the Conqueror
description: Story of William's corpse, inhabited by a demon trapped by his botched funeral rite.

name: The Conquered Bastard
description: Infernal Lore tractatus (Quality 6) describing the demon in William's corpse.

name: Priory of St Gervais
description: Priory in Rouen where William the Conqueror died.

name: Hague-Dicke
description: Ninth-century Norse earthwork cutting off the northwest Cotentin, now ruined and rumored to hide buried loot.

name: Barfleur
description: Harbor town where William's invasion fleet was built, haunted by maritime ghosts including a spectral fleet.

name: William son of Henry I
description: Son of Henry I of England, drowned leaving Barfleur in 1120.

name: Avranches
description: Small county and diocesan town on Normandy's border with Brittany.

name: Mont St. Michael
description: Benedictine monastery founded by the archangel Michael; enters a Divine regio (aura 8) at high tide.

name: Archangel Michael
description: Archangel who appeared to Aubert in 708 and founded Mont St. Michael; wants to supplant Hermetic magic with a Divine variant.

name: Aubert
description: Bishop of Avranches who built the chapel on Mont St. Michael; his relics include a skull holed by the archangel.

name: House Diedne
description: Destroyed Hermetic House whose precursors used Mount Tombe; had covenants in Normandy and knew a regio at Clermont.

name: Richard I, Duke of Normandy
description: Duke who sponsored colonization of Mont St. Michael by Benedictines in 966.

name: Abbot Maynard
description: Leader of the monks from St. Wandrille who colonized Mont St. Michael.

name: Abbot Hildebert
description: Abbot who began additions to Mont St. Michael in 1020.

name: Abbot Jordan
description: Abbot who began reconstruction of Mont St. Michael in 1210.

name: Fen Ague
description: Disease contracted in the Cotentin swamps causing a Heavy Wound, chills and fever.

name: Apparitio Sancti Michaelis Archangelis in Monte Tumba
description: Anonymous Divine Lore tractatus (Quality 11) on the foundation of Mont St. Michael.

name: Holy Magic Theory summa
description: Untitled book found in a crypt beneath Mont St. Michael; its reader is visited by the archangel Michael.

name: Holy Magic Theory
description: Divine variant of Magic Theory taught by the book in the Uncovered Crypt story seed.

name: Hermetic Raiding
description: Tradition of covenants raiding each other, established largely by Montverte and upheld by Tribunal precedent.

name: Five Great Lieges
description: The five major liege covenants of the Normandy Tribunal, of which Montverte is one.

name: Haland
description: Ungifted Viking warrior, elder brother of Harivald, ancestor of the lords of Montverte.

name: Harivald
description: Viking sorcerer, founder of Montverte and of a Flambeau lineage.

name: House Ex Miscellanea
description: House into which Harivald was first inducted.

name: House Flambeau
description: House of martial magi that dominates Montverte's council.

name: House Tremere
description: House whose martial magi rallied at Montverte in the Schism War.

name: Lords of Montverte
description: Noble family descended from Haland, dominated by the magi of Montverte.

name: Baron of Montverte
description: Mundane lord of Montverte castle, unwittingly controlled by the covenant's magi.

name: Koilios
description: Magus of Montverte whose raid on Lapis Crudus established a precedent legalizing raiding.

name: Lapis Crudus
description: Covenant raided by Koilios; a vassal of Sinapis.

name: Laon
description: Mount in Picardy that inspired Montverte's construction.

name: Inner Council of Montverte
description: Secretive council of five elder magi ruling Montverte, led by Geirlaug.

name: Geirlaug
description: Ancient Twilight-ridden Flambeau Archmaga and leader of Montverte, master of Ignem who appears in a council mirror.

name: Council Mirror
description: Great mirror at the head of Montverte's council table in which Geirlaug appears.

name: Oleron
description: Merinita covenant in the Apple Mile regio on the island of Oleron, descended from an Arthurian faerie court.

name: Thormod
description: Flambeau filius of Geirlaug, Montverte's cold Hermetic ambassador and secretly a member of the Children of Odin.

name: Eduardus
description: Tytalus magus apprenticed in Jerbiton, steward of Montverte under the persona Edward; a member of the purple Fideli.

name: House Tytalus
description: House Eduardus joined; in internal struggle, and disliked by Caprican.

name: House Jerbiton
description: House in which Eduardus was apprenticed.

name: Gentle Gift
description: Virtue removing the social penalty of The Gift, possessed by Eduardus and Rotgiers.

name: Enchanted Baron's Chair
description: Centuries-old high chair enchanted with a Mentem effect to ensure the baron's compliance; slightly Warps its occupants.

name: Purple Fideli
description: Faction of House Tytalus backing Buliste as the true Prima.

name: Buliste
description: Claimant supported by the purple Fideli as true Prima of House Tytalus.

name: Hippian school
description: School of thought within House Tytalus that Eduardus supports.

name: Children of Odin
description: Mystery Cult practicing Viking magic, whose hierophant is Queen Skuld; Thormod is a member.

name: Queen Skuld
description: Hierophant of the Children of Odin.

name: Viking Magic
description: Magic practiced by the Children of Odin, learned by Thormod.

name: Waddenzee
description: Pirate covenant of the Rhine Tribunal on an island north of Flanders allied with Montverte.

name: Lotharingian Tribunal
description: Proposed new Tribunal to be founded by seceding Normandy covenants, which Montverte aims to thwart.

name: Rotgiers de Gerberoy
description: Senior Tremere magus of Montverte, knightly warrior and Tourney champion responsible for martial affairs and raiding.

name: Simo
description: Ancient warhorse, familiar of Rotgiers de Gerberoy.

name: Tourney
description: The Normandy Tribunal's tournament with joust and certamen contests.

name: Certamen
description: Hermetic magical duel; a Tourney contest and sufficient for Oleron's champion challenge.

name: Rotgiers' Talisman Mace
description: Ornate bejewelled mace enchanted as Rotgiers' talisman.

name: The Gift
description: Virtue possessed by Rotgiers de Gerberoy of House Tremere.

name: Hermetic Magus
description: Virtue possessed by Rotgiers de Gerberoy of House Tremere.

name: Affinity with Rego
description: Virtue possessed by Rotgiers de Gerberoy of House Tremere.

name: Affinity with Terram
description: Virtue possessed by Rotgiers de Gerberoy of House Tremere.

name: Cautious Sorcerer
description: Virtue possessed by Rotgiers de Gerberoy of House Tremere.

name: Improved Characteristics
description: Virtue possessed by Rotgiers de Gerberoy of House Tremere.

name: Large
description: Virtue possessed by Rotgiers de Gerberoy of House Tremere.

name: Minor Magical Focus
description: Virtue possessed by Rotgiers de Gerberoy of House Tremere.

name: Puissant Single Weapon
description: Virtue possessed by Rotgiers de Gerberoy of House Tremere.

name: Subtle Magic
description: Virtue possessed by Rotgiers de Gerberoy of House Tremere.

name: Feud
description: Flaw possessed by Rotgiers de Gerberoy of House Tremere.

name: Proud
description: Flaw possessed by Rotgiers de Gerberoy of House Tremere.

name: Deficient Form
description: Flaw possessed by Rotgiers de Gerberoy of House Tremere.

name: Driven
description: Flaw possessed by Rotgiers de Gerberoy of House Tremere.

name: Poor Hearing
description: Flaw possessed by Rotgiers de Gerberoy of House Tremere.

name: Susceptibility to Faerie Power
description: Flaw possessed by Rotgiers de Gerberoy of House Tremere.

description: Ability appearing in the lutin's statistics.

description: Ability appearing in the lutin's statistics.

description: Ability appearing in the lutin's statistics.

description: Ability appearing in the lutin's statistics.

description: Ability appearing in the lutin's statistics.

description: Ability appearing in the lutin's statistics.

name: Swim
description: Ability appearing in the lutin's statistics.

name: Animal Handling
description: Ability appearing in Rotgiers de Gerberoy's statistics.

name: Artes Liberales
description: Ability appearing in Rotgiers de Gerberoy's statistics.

name: Code of Hermes
description: Ability appearing in Rotgiers de Gerberoy's statistics.

name: Concentration
description: Ability appearing in Rotgiers de Gerberoy's statistics.

description: Ability appearing in Rotgiers de Gerberoy's statistics.

description: Ability appearing in Rotgiers de Gerberoy's statistics.

description: Ability appearing in Rotgiers de Gerberoy's statistics.

description: Ability appearing in Rotgiers de Gerberoy's statistics.

description: Ability appearing in Rotgiers de Gerberoy's statistics.

description: Ability appearing in Rotgiers de Gerberoy's statistics.

name: Order of Hermes Lore
description: Ability appearing in Rotgiers de Gerberoy's statistics.

name: Parma Magica
description: Ability appearing in Rotgiers de Gerberoy's statistics.

description: Ability appearing in Rotgiers de Gerberoy's statistics.

name: Philosophiae
description: Ability appearing in Rotgiers de Gerberoy's statistics.

name: Ride
description: Ability appearing in Rotgiers de Gerberoy's statistics.

name: Single Weapon
description: Ability appearing in Rotgiers de Gerberoy's statistics.

name: Teaching
description: Ability appearing in Rotgiers de Gerberoy's statistics.

name: French
description: Ability appearing in Rotgiers de Gerberoy's statistics.

name: Infernal Lore
description: Ability covered by tractatus such as The Conquered Bastard.

name: Divine Lore
description: Ability covered by Contra Haereticos and the Apparitio.

name: Theology
description: Ability covered by De Laude Sanctorum.

name: Civil and Canon Law
description: Ability covered by Liber Regularum and Orderic Vitalis.

name: Organization Lore
description: Ability; Decem Libri Historiarum includes Organization Lore: Frankish Royalty.

name: Magic Lore
description: Ability covered in Decem Libri Historiarum.

name: Church Lore
description: Ability covered in Gregory of Tours' works.

name: Dominion Lore
description: Ability covered in Books on the Miracles of St. Martin.

name: Piercing Lance of Bone
description: CrAn 20 spell creating a sharpened lance of hardened bone in the caster's hand.

name: Soothe Pains of the Beast
description: CrAn 20 spell known by Rotgiers.

name: The Wizard's Mount
description: CrAn 20 spell known by Rotgiers.

name: Beast of Outlandish Size
description: MuAn 15 spell known by Rotgiers.

name: Agony of the Beast
description: PeAn 15 spell known by Rotgiers.

name: Commanding the Harnessed Beast
description: ReAn 30 spell known by Rotgiers.

name: Purification of the Festering Wounds
description: CrCo 20 spell known by Rotgiers.

name: Preternatural Growth and Shrinking
description: MuCo 15 spell known by Rotgiers.

name: Gift of the Bear's Fortitude
description: MuCo 25 spell known by Rotgiers.

name: Grip of the Choking Hand
description: PeCo 25 spell known by Rotgiers.

name: Stance of the Firm-Buttocked Knight
description: ReCo 20 spell preventing the caster falling from a seat or saddle.

name: The Leap of Homecoming
description: ReCo 30 spell known by Rotgiers.

name: Posing the Silent Question
description: InMe 20 spell known by Rotgiers.

name: Aura of Rightful Authority
description: ReMe 20 spell known by Rotgiers.

name: Wall of Protecting Stone
description: CrTe 25 spell known by Rotgiers.

name: Edge of the Razor
description: MuTe 20 spell known by Rotgiers.

name: Crest of the Earth Wave
description: ReTe 20 spell known by Rotgiers.

name: The Unerring Lance
description: ReTe 20 spell making a thrusting weapon move only directly forward, so it can only be dodged.

name: The Earth Split Asunder
description: ReTe 30 spell known by Rotgiers.

name: Demon's Eternal Oblivion
description: PeVi 20 spell known by Rotgiers.

name: Wind of Mundane Silence
description: PeVi 25 spell Rotgiers casts silently against opponents' magical defenses.

name: Maintaining the Demanding Spell
description: ReVi 30 spell known by Rotgiers.

name: Spell Mastery
description: Mastery of spells granting options such as Penetration, Fast Casting, Multiple Casting and Quiet Casting.

name: Twilight
description: Hermetic state; Geirlaug has spent many years in Twilight and Rotgiers bears Twilight Scars.

name: Twilight Scars
description: Lasting effects of Twilight; Rotgiers' include instilling fear and deafness to compliments.

name: Warping
description: Magical distortion; Rotgiers has a Warping Score and the baron's chair Warps its occupants.

name: Familiar
description: Bonded magical animal companion, such as Rotgiers' warhorse Simo and Runild's black cat.

name: Talisman
description: Magus' personal enchanted item; Rotgiers' mace.

name: Arcane Connection
description: Magical link used by Rotgiers against opponents; each of the Three Spears is one to the others.

name: Sympathetic Connection
description: Magical bonus linking an object to a target, as the Bayeux tapestry does.

name: Runild
description: Youngest Tremere member of Montverte's inner council, overseeing its library, vis and junior labwork; her familiar is a black cat.

name: Jerbiton
description: Founder of House Jerbiton, whose familiar's lineage includes Runild's black cat.

name: Redcap
description: Messenger magi of House Mercere; Montverte likely has one and Redcaps lived at Alcuin's Auberge.

name: Grogs
description: Covenant soldiers; Montverte's are numerous and well equipped.

name: Covenfolk
description: Covenant servants; at Montverte they are the baron's household.

name: House Bonisagus
description: House whose magi suit Montverte.

name: House Verditius
description: House of item-making magi; Quintinus refuses its status games.

name: House Merinita
description: Faerie-focused House; Oleron's magi are Merinita.

name: House Bjornaer
description: House whose Clan Ilfetu knows of an ancestor-site cave near the Vézère.

name: Clan Ilfetu
description: Clan of House Bjornaer knowing an ancestor site in the Vézère valley.

name: Ancestor Site
description: Cave suitable for House Bjornaer rituals.

name: Creo
description: Hermetic Art referenced in this text (vis, spells or magical focus).

name: Intellego
description: Hermetic Art referenced in this text (vis, spells or magical focus).

name: Muto
description: Hermetic Art referenced in this text (vis, spells or magical focus).

name: Perdo
description: Hermetic Art referenced in this text (vis, spells or magical focus).

description: Hermetic Art referenced in this text (vis, spells or magical focus).

description: Hermetic Art referenced in this text (vis, spells or magical focus).

name: Ignem
description: Hermetic Art referenced in this text (vis, spells or magical focus).

name: Imaginem
description: Hermetic Art referenced in this text (vis, spells or magical focus).

name: Mentem
description: Hermetic Art referenced in this text (vis, spells or magical focus).

name: Terram
description: Hermetic Art referenced in this text (vis, spells or magical focus).

name: Vim
description: Hermetic Art referenced in this text (vis, spells or magical focus).

name: Vis
description: Raw magical power in pawns, found in many sources across Normandy, Anjou and Aquitaine.

name: Tropaea
description: Vis gathered from the Auvergne hot springs and gases.

name: Magic Aura
description: Aura of the Magic realm found at many megaliths and sites.

name: Faerie Aura
description: Aura of the Faerie realm, e.g. Faeries' Cave and the Apple Mile.

name: Divine Aura
description: Aura of the Divine, e.g. Mont St. Michael's regio.

name: Dominion
description: The Divine realm's influence, whose aura swamps pagan Magic auras.

name: Magic Realm
description: Realm of Power of Magic, whose auras are found at pagan sites.

name: Faerie Realm
description: Realm of faeries, whose courts and regiones appear throughout Normandy and Oleron.

name: Divine Realm
description: Realm of the Divine; Michael wants a Divine variant of Hermetic magic.

name: Infernal Realm
description: Realm of demons, such as the demon in William's corpse.

name: Regio
description: Supernatural area of a place with multiple levels, such as the Apple Mile and Mont St. Michael at high tide.

name: Faith Score
description: Measure of Divine power of relics, e.g. Holy Thorn and Girdle of the Virgin.

name: Mystery Cult
description: Secret initiatory society, such as the Children of Odin.

name: Mystery of Becoming
description: Mystery preferred by faerie magi to becoming minor faeries in Stone Couches.

name: Wizard's War
description: Hermetic sanctioned conflict Caprican is willing to use against Tytalus.

name: Archmage
description: Title of an especially accomplished magus; Geirlaug is an Archmaga.

name: Voting Sigil
description: Tribunal voting token; Rotgiers holds most Tremere sigils and Runild lacks her own.

name: Anjou
description: Region of the counties of Anjou, Touraine and Maine, formerly Angevin, now held by the French crown.

name: Aquitaine
description: Largest duchy in France; its northern part lies in the Normandy Tribunal.

name: Angevin Dynasty
description: Dynasty that ruled Anjou and Aquitaine in conflict with France.

name: Touraine
description: County forming part of Anjou.

name: Maine
description: County/duchy forming part of Anjou; capital Le Mans.

name: Fulk Nerra
description: Count of Anjou 987-1040, founder of Ronceray abbey.

name: Henry II of England
description: Count of Anjou who became King of England; founded Angers' Hospital of St. John and died at Chinon.

name: Angers
description: Capital of Anjou on the River Maine, center of Plantagenet power.

name: Béhuard Island
description: Loire island with an oratory over a sea-goddess shrine, where a Dominion aura swamps a level-2 Magic aura.

name: Abbey of Ronceray
description: Abbey in Angers founded by Fulk Nerra.

name: Chinon
description: Town on the River Vienne with a great castle built by Henry II; given to Philip II by the Treaty of Chinon.

name: Treaty of Chinon
description: 1214 treaty giving Chinon to Philip II.

name: Isabelle of Angoulême
description: Countess of Angoulême, widow of King John, betrothed to Hugh X of Lusignan.

name: Atsingani
description: Current covenant in Anjou and Aquitaine.

name: Nidi
description: The only covenant in Aquitaine, predating the 1103 Grand Tribunal ruling.

name: Alcuin's Auberge
description: Redcap Mercer House in Tours, fallen to raiders in 1197.

name: Ligurio
description: Ruined vassal covenant of Fudarus in the Vendée marshes.

name: Nauche-Fleur
description: Ruined or lost covenant of Anjou and Aquitaine.

name: Sinapis
description: Powerful covenant founded in 855 at Tavant, abandoned in 1063; parent of Aedes Salii, Lapis Crudus and Rothomagus.

name: Vexatores
description: Ruined or lost covenant of Anjou and Aquitaine.

name: Tavant
description: Village with a painted church, the only remnant of the covenant of Sinapis.

name: Le Mans
description: Capital of Maine with the Cathedral of St. Julien and a pagan fertility menhir.

name: Le Mans Menhir
description: Pinkish menhir by Le Mans cathedral, former fertility cult center whose sacrificial blood yields Creo vis.

name: Holy Thorn
description: Thorn from Christ's crown at the Abbey of St. Peter at Solesmes, Faith score 2.

name: Abbey of St. Peter at Solesmes
description: Abbey owning a Holy Thorn.

name: Seeker
description: Magus who investigates ancient magic, who might study the Le Mans menhir.

name: Tours
description: City on the Loire with the Basilica of St. Martin, site of the Redcap Mercer House Alcuin's Auberge.

name: Basilica of St. Martin
description: Pilgrimage basilica in Tours where St. Martin is interred.

name: Mercer House
description: Redcap waystation; Alcuin's Auberge in Tours was one.

name: Lixivia
description: Covenant that disbanded in poverty in 1124, preceding Alcuin's Auberge.

name: Fudarus
description: Tytalus covenant, now nearly empty; suspected of sending raiders against Alcuin's Auberge.

name: Mercurian Magicians
description: Roman magicians of Mercury, for whom a tower near Tours was built.

name: Gallo-Roman Tower of Tours
description: Windowless Roman brick tower west of Tours with Magic aura 1 at base and 5 at top.

name: Azay-le-Rideau
description: Village near cave settlements; a valley south of it has a level 4 Magic aura and Aquam vis.

name: Faeries' Cave
description: Dolmen northwest of Tours with a Faerie aura of 3 rising to 5 when fae feast there.

name: Saint Martin
description: Bishop of Tours and founder of the Abbey of Ligugé.

name: Marmoutier
description: Monastery by Tours' gate where St. Martin lived.

name: Gregory of Tours
description: Bishop of Tours from 573 and author of historical and theological books.

name: Decem Libri Historiarum
description: History of the Franks by Gregory of Tours with several summae.

name: Lives of the Fathers
description: Church Lore tractatus by Gregory of Tours.

name: Books on the Miracles of St. Martin
description: Dominion Lore tractatus by Gregory of Tours.

name: On the Courses of the Stars
description: Tractatus by Gregory of Tours on Astronomy and Church Lore.

name: Merovingian Dynasty
description: Frankish rulers said to have supernatural powers, founded by Merovech.

name: Alcuin of York
description: Adviser to Charlemagne who became abbot of St. Martin's Abbey in Tours.

name: Charlemagne
description: Emperor who founded the kingdom of Aquitaine and Brantôme abbey; Ogier was his paladin.

name: Samur
description: Town grown around a monastery for St. Florent's relics, hosting tournaments in July.

name: Gennes
description: Place with a Roman amphitheatre beside a Magic regio of nymphs.

name: Nymphs
description: Nymphs living in a Gallo-Roman shrine regio at Gennes who give Aquam vis.

name: Dolmen of Bagneux
description: Largest dolmen in the Samur region with a low Magic aura.

name: Abbey of Fontevraud
description: Double abbey under an abbess housing the Plantagenet tombs; Eleanor of Aquitaine is buried there.

name: Eleanor of Aquitaine
description: Duchess who married Louis then Henry, buried at Fontevraud in 1204.

name: Doué-la-Fontaine
description: Site of rock containing Creo vis with power to preserve flesh.

name: Girdle of the Virgin
description: Relic at Le Puy-Notre-Dame aiding childbirth, Faith score 1.

name: Le Puy-Notre-Dame
description: Pilgrim church housing the Girdle of the Virgin.

name: Vendôme
description: Town on the River Loir with the Abbey of the Trinity.

name: Abbey of the Trinity
description: Powerful abbey in Vendôme founded by Geoffroy Martel.

name: Geoffroy Martel
description: Count of Anjou who founded the Abbey of the Trinity in 1032.

name: Arm of St. George
description: Relic with Faith score 2 at Vendôme.

name: Tear of Christ
description: Relic with Faith score 3 donated to the Abbey of the Trinity.

name: Three Spears
description: Legendary flaming spears of Vendôme, Arcane Connections to each other that drip Divine-tainted Ignem vis when reunited.

name: John IV of Montoire
description: Count living in Vendôme castle who owns one of the spears.

name: Trôo
description: Village with cave homes in the Loir valley.

name: Central Massif
description: Volcanic highland in eastern Aquitaine.

name: Grand Tribunal
description: Hermetic body whose 1103 ruling shaped the Normandy Tribunal's borders.

name: Provençal Tribunal
description: Tribunal to which new covenants south of the Dordogne belong.

name: Vendée
description: Thinly populated northwest corner of Aquitaine of forest, moor and marsh.

name: Mount Mercury
description: Highest point in the Vendée with a church on a Mercury shrine, a Redcap pilgrimage site.

name: Mercury
description: Roman god, patron of travelers, honored by Redcaps.

name: St. Hilary
description: Bishop of Poitiers who trapped a flood demon under the sea.

name: Trapped Vendée Demon
description: Demon trapped in a sea cave by St. Hilary, bellowing at high tide.

name: Noirmoutier
description: Island with a level 3 Magic aura and a druidess beach at level 5.

name: La Rochelle
description: Chartered port held by England with a Templar church.

name: Templars
description: Knightly order owning a church at La Rochelle.

name: Poitiers
description: Ecclesiastic city with the Baptistery of St. John and Church of St. Hilary.

name: Abbey of Ligugé
description: Oldest monastery in the west, founded by St. Martin in 361.

name: Charles Martel
description: Defeated the Moors at the battle of Poitiers.

name: Lusignan
description: Castle built by faerie magic, where Mélusine appears.

name: Mélusine
description: Female water sprite of Lusignan cursed to be half serpent on the Sabbath; wife of Raymond.

name: Raymond
description: Adopted son of the Count of Poitiers who married Mélusine.

name: Parthenay
description: Castle conjured by Mélusine for her second son.

name: Undine Blood
description: Virtue shared by descendants of Mélusine.

name: Bougon Tumuli
description: Six hidden burial mounds forming an undiscovered pagan necropolis, likely haunted.

name: Angoulême
description: Walled city with the castle of Isabella, Countess of Angoulême.

name: Hugh X of Lusignan
description: Count of La Marche, betrothed to Isabella.

name: Chassenon
description: Roman city ruins with baths whose healing water has Creo vis.

name: Limoges
description: City divided between the Cité and the commercial center around the Abbey of St. Martial.

name: St. Martial
description: Converter of the Limoges region, buried at the abbey bearing his name.

name: St. Eligius
description: Goldsmith and adviser to Dagobert I who founded Solignac monastery.

name: St. Léonard
description: Godson of Clovis, hermit at Noblat.

name: Saintes
description: Regional capital on the Charente with the Arch of Germanicus.

name: St-Èmilion
description: Wine town ruled by the Jurade with an underground church.

name: Jurade
description: Citizen assembly governing St-Èmilion.

name: Geoffroy of Rudel
description: Troubadour devoted to Countess Hodierna of Tripoli.

name: Lanterns of the Dead
description: Cemetery towers with lanterns; an angel pulls down those over unworthy dead.

name: Le Cité
description: Capital of Périgord, with the sacred spring Vésone and St. Stephen's Cathedral.

name: Vésone
description: Sacred spring source of Aquam vis.

name: St Front
description: Converter of Périgord who slew the dragon La Coloubre.

name: Le Puy-St-Front
description: Town rival to Le Cité.

name: Brantôme
description: Abbey town with the Fountain of the Rock.

name: Aubeterre-sur-Dronne
description: Town with a monolithic church.

name: Pierre de Castillon
description: Crusader who brought relics to Aubeterre.

name: Hautefort
description: Castle of the de Born family.

name: Bertrand de Born
description: Troubadour with supernatural musical gift.

name: Constantine de Born
description: Bertrand's brother who ruined Hautefort, possibly by magic.

name: Way of St. James
description: Pilgrim route to Santiago de Compostela through Anjou and Aquitaine.

name: Santiago de Compostela
description: Great pilgrimage destination in Spain.

name: Bergerac
description: Wine port on the Dordogne.

name: La Coloubre
description: Dragon near Lalinde slain by St. Front.

name: Truffles
description: Rare vis-bearing fungus containing Herbam vis.

name: Vézère
description: River valley with Magic aura and painted caves leading to a regio.

name: St. Christopher's Rock
description: Cliff settlement in the Vézère valley.

name: Clermont
description: City on a former druid wood with a regio of Terram vis, ruled by its Lord Bishop.

name: Montferrand
description: Town around the Count of Auvergne's castle, rival of Clermont.

name: La Chaise-Dieu
description: Monastery of St. Robert heading over 200 priories.

name: Puy de Dôme
description: Volcano with a shrine to Lug, Mercury and St. Barnabas, and a temple of Mercury regio.

name: Lug
description: Pagan god originally honored on the Puy de Dôme.

name: Lake Pavin
description: Lake where a basalt stone summons a storm yielding Auram vis.

name: Bort-les-Orgues
description: Site of Rego and Imaginem vis.

name: Auvergne Fire Elemental
description: Powerful fire elemental dwelling deep underground, source of hot springs.

name: Apple Mile
description: Faerie regio (aura 5) on Oleron island where the covenant lies, always summer.

name: Oleron Island
description: Small island in the Bay of Biscay containing the Apple Mile.

name: King Arthur
description: Legendary king whose knights challenged Lanval.

name: Lanval
description: Arthurian knight and champion of Oleron defeated by Kherion in 1028.

name: Triamour
description: Faerie Queen of Oleron who won Lanval.

name: Faerie Queen of Oleron
description: Faerie queen embodying the Apple Mile, succeeded by her daughter at each challenge.

name: Kherion of Merinita
description: Magus who defeated Lanval in 1028.

name: Caprican of Merinita
description: Leader and champion of Oleron, with Strong Faun Blood, hostile to Tytalus.

name: Stone Couches
description: Faerie tumuli that grow duplicates of folk heroes, called Sleepers.

name: Sleepers
description: Faerie duplicates of folk heroes grown in Stone Couches.

name: Queen's Champion
description: Consort ruling the Apple Mile, won by challenge on Midsummer's Day.

name: Oberon
description: Dwarf-king Sleeper awakened at Oleron, with a magic horn.

name: Alberich
description: Magician brother of Merovech.

name: Merovech
description: Founder of the Merovingian Dynasty.

name: Arcadia
description: Faerie realm sought by Oleron's magi.

name: Huon of Bordeaux
description: Hero of a song aided by Oberon.

name: Oberon's Horn
description: Horn banishing hunger, curing sickness and summoning people.

name: Faerie Queen of Avalon
description: Faerie who permanently woke Oberon.

name: Morgana Le Fay
description: Enchantress said to be Oberon's mother and Ogier's captor.

name: Julius Caesar
description: Said to be Oberon's father.

name: Lysette
description: Caprican's wife, the faerie queen.

name: Columbine
description: Caprican's infant daughter.

name: Strong Faun Blood
description: Virtue possessed by Caprican.

name: Keepers of a Thousand Tales
description: Group focused on Arabic stories, of which Caprican is a member.

name: Ushant
description: Location near Oleron associated with House Tytalus.

name: Amelie of Merinita
description: Oleron spokeswoman, focused on Aquam with river-nymph blood.

name: Quintinus of Verditius
description: Verditius magus who constructs new Stone Couches.

name: Ogier the Dane
description: Charlemagne's paladin carried to Avalon by Morgana le Fay.

name: Avalon
description: Isle where Morgana kept Ogier.

name: Ogier's Ring
description: Magic rejuvenating ring given to Ogier by Morgana.

name: Crown of Forgetfulness
description: Crown Morgana placed on Ogier.
